test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain amount of money for 1¹/₂ years at an interest rate of 10% per annum is ₹183, when the interest is compounded semi-annually, determine the principal amount.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **semi-annual** compounding, **Rate** = 10% ÷ 2 = 5% and **Time** = 1.5 × 2 = 3 periods.

Using the **Ratio Method** for 3 periods (3 : 3 : 1), the difference (CI − SI) is represented by the last two parts: 3 × (Interest on Interest) + 1 × (Interest on that).

Let **Principal** = 20³ = 8000 units (since 5% = 1/20).

Difference = 3 × (5% of 400) + 1 × (5% of 20) = 3 × 20 + 1 = 61 units.

61 units = ₹183 → 1 unit = ₹3.

**∴ Principal** = 8000 × 3 = ₹24000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Annual Rate = 10%, Time = 1.5 years, Difference (CI − SI) = ₹183.

**Formula Used:**

For 3 periods, Difference (D) = P × (r/100)² × (3 + r/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3035d971494d8eb3ef4fc7cf5f7e03ac595435689cfc66fd2331d09e7ca1ebad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Semi-annual rate (r) = 10% ÷ 2 = 5%

⇒ Number of periods (n) = 1.5 × 2 = 3

⇒ 183 = P × (5/100)² × (3 + 5/100)

⇒ 183 = P × (1/20)² × (3 + 1/20)

⇒ 183 = P × (1/400) × (61/20)

⇒ 183 = P × (61/8000)

⇒ P = (183 × 8000) ÷ 61

⇒ P = 3 × 8000

⇒ P = 24000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹24000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference for 2 Years/Periods

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by D = P(R/100)².

Effective Rate of Interest

When interest is compounded semi-annually, the effective annual rate is Rₑff = [ (1 + R/200)² − 1 ] × 100.

Compounding Frequency

As the frequency of compounding increases (quarterly, monthly), the Compound Interest increases while Simple Interest remains the same.
